title: Put PLINK 2 in bin/

blocks.what_we_do:
Get the latest matching build from the [official PLINK 2 page](https://www.cog-genomics.org/plink/2.0/). A build is a version of the program made for one system and processor. Follow these actions:

1. Open the page. It lists several downloads. Choose the build whose name matches your system and processor from step 0.1. The names on the page can change.
2. Save the ZIP file. A ZIP file is one compressed file that holds other files.
3. Extract the ZIP file. On Windows, right-click it, choose "Extract All", then click "Extract". On macOS, double-click it.
4. Inside you find the program. It is `plink2.exe` on Windows and `plink2` on macOS or Linux. This file is the [executable](docs/glossary.md#executable), the file your computer can run.
5. Copy the executable into the `bin/` folder of the course project. The project was created at step 0.3. The ZIP file may hold other programs too. Copy only `plink2.exe` (or `plink2`).

The ZIP file is not the executable, so extract it first. When you finish, you should see `plink2.exe` or `plink2` inside the `bin` folder.

Choose a build from the official download table:

| System and processor | Build |
| --- | --- |
| Windows x64, AVX2 support confirmed | Windows AVX2 |
| Windows x64, AVX2 unknown or unavailable | Windows 64-bit |
| Windows 32-bit | Windows 32-bit |
| macOS Apple Silicon, including M1 and later | macOS M1 |
| macOS Intel, AVX2 support confirmed | macOS AVX2 |
| macOS Intel, AVX2 unknown or unavailable | macOS 64-bit |
| Linux x86_64, AVX2 support confirmed | Linux AVX2 Intel or AMD, matching the processor vendor |
| Linux x86_64, AVX2 unknown or unavailable | Linux 64-bit Intel |
| Linux 32-bit x86 | Linux 32-bit |

AVX2 is a processor instruction set. If you are unsure, choose the matching 64-bit build without AVX2. The official page does not list a native Windows ARM or Linux ARM download; ask support for a compatible build. Do not use a macOS M1 build on another system.
blocks.why: PLINK 2 reads the genotype file formats. It computes [quality control](docs/glossary.md#quality-control) (QC) and association statistics. QC means checks that find samples or data that cannot be trusted. PLINK 1.9 is a different program, so it does not replace PLINK 2. The tested version is stored in one place, the settings file `config.R`. The setup check reports your version and warns you if it differs.
blocks.you_need: Your system and processor from step 0.1, and the extracted project from step 0.3. You may download the executable first and copy it after you extract the project.
blocks.command: No R code to run. Check that you extracted the ZIP and found `plink2.exe` on Windows, or `plink2` on macOS or Linux. Copy it into the project's `bin` folder after step 0.3. The setup check at step 0.8 reports the tested and installed versions.
blocks.expected_result: The extracted executable is named `plink2.exe` on Windows, or `plink2` on macOS or Linux. At step 0.8 your executable must identify itself as PLINK v2. A different build gives a warning. A different version number alone does not make the check fail.
blocks.troubleshooting:
On macOS or Linux, the extracted file may lack permission to run. Open a terminal in the project folder (the project root). Type `chmod u+x bin/plink2`. This command gives your user permission to run that file. If your institution's security blocks it, ask support. Do not switch off computer security controls.

On macOS, Gatekeeper may block the official downloaded executable. After the blocked attempt, open System Settings, then Privacy & Security. Find the message for `plink2` and click "Open Anyway", then confirm "Open". Follow [Apple's instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102445). Retry step 0.8.

On Windows, SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC" for a downloaded executable. For the file you obtained from the official PLINK page, review "More info" and use "Run anyway" if your institution permits it. If that option is unavailable, ask support. See [Microsoft's SmartScreen guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/smartscreen-reputation).
blocks.quick_check:
Can a file named `plink2.zip` be used as the executable?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>No. Extract the matching executable from it.</details>
blocks.files_created: `bin/plink2.exe` or `bin/plink2`. It stays outside [Git](docs/glossary.md#git), the tool that records versions of the project files.
